items.title: Exercise 4.1 · Distance lower bound for gradient-span algorithms

source.anchor: §4.2, Exercise 4.1 (printed/PDF p. 28); Definition 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 (p. 26), path quadratic and prefix induction (p. 27), affine minimizer (pp. 27–28); Definition 1.12, Eq. (1.7) (p. 11)
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Lectures on Optimization. Original ASTIS restatement and solution; no textbook prose copied or endorsement implied.

items.statement: Let D and N be natural numbers with 1 ≤ N and 2N+1 ≤ D, let β>0, and prescribe x₀∈ℝᴰ. For v=y−x₀ use the translated path quadratic below and let x★ have centered coordinates 1−k/(D+1), k=1,…,D. The witness is convex, C¹ and satisfies the β quadratic upper model; x★ minimizes it. Every sequence with initial value x₀ and each centered next iterate in the real span of the preceding actual gradients retains at least 1/8 of its initial squared distance to x★ at step N.
assumptions: D,N are natural numbers, 1 ≤ N and 2N+1 ≤ D; β>0 and the start x₀ are fixed before the run.

Use the real Euclidean norm and the genuine gradient of the explicit quadratic. The algorithm premise is exactly the affine gradient-span rule on each trajectory; class membership and minimization are conclusions.

formulae.label: The fixed witness and chosen minimizer

obligations.label: Use the same translated path quadratic and certify convexity, continuous differentiability, and the global upper model.
Prove minimization for the stated affine profile.
Propagate the real affine span restriction and prove the untouched-tail distance comparison.

bindings.boundary: The statement uses the very same finite path quadratic and affine minimizer for every allowed run at a prescribed start. The explicit factor 1/8 is a proved universal choice, not attributed to the text or claimed sharp. This is a squared-distance comparison for gradient-span trajectories, not the function-value lower bound, Exercise 4.2, or a theorem about unrestricted deterministic or randomized oracle access.

assumption_deltas.lean: Fin (d+1) as coordinate type, 1 ≤ N and 2*N+1 ≤ d+1.
assumption_deltas.reason: D=d+1 with positive dimension, natural indices and the equivalent integer inequality.

assumption_deltas.source: β>0, fixed arbitrary start, convex β-smooth witness.
assumption_deltas.lean: The literal translated source polynomial; ConvexOn, ContDiff ℝ 1 and the exact upper quadratic model are outputs.
assumption_deltas.reason: This exposes both parts of Definition 1.12, not an extra caller regularity premise.

assumption_deltas.source: Definition 4.3: deterministic algorithm generates an affine-gradient-span trajectory.
assumption_deltas.lean: Quantify over sequences starting at x₀ whose next centered iterate belongs to the real linear span of actual previous gradients.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source run-level condition is used at each index; there is no theorem about querying outside that span.

assumption_deltas.source: Distance comparison up to an absolute constant for the same witness.
assumption_deltas.lean: Explicit universal 1/8 and the affine minimizer of that witness.
assumption_deltas.reason: One valid constant is realized by the untouched-tail estimate; no claimed sharpness.
